消.meaning: A candle flame flickers, and its shadow on the wall bears a <part>resemblance</part> to a little dancer. You flick <part>water drops</part> at it: hiss! The dancer shrinks, wobbles and is gone. You've managed to <kanji>extinguish</kanji> it.
消.on: Whoops: that candle was the only light for the puppet <sound>show</sound>.
消.kun: In the dark, you grope around for the <sound>key</sound> to the light box.

少.meaning: A jar of sweets holds just a <part>little</part> pile, and every time you walk past, a sneaky hand makes a <part>slash</part> through it and grabs one. Soon only three are left… then two. Very <kanji>few</kanji>.
少.on: The very last sweet gets its own <sound>show</sound> under a spotlight before someone eats it.
少.kun: A <sound>su</sound>shi chef hands a hungry <sound>ko</sound>ala just one grain of rice.

運.meaning: An <part>army</part> of ants marches up a <part>ramp</part>, each one hauling a crumb ten times its size. Up and over, up and over, until the whole picnic is gone. They <kanji>carry</kanji> it all home.
運.on: The smallest ant of all carries a whole sp<sound>oon</sound> up the ramp on its back.
運.kun: The ants drop every crumb at a <sound>hu</sound>t, where a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala eats the lot.

信.meaning: A stranger hangs his hat on your <part>coat hook</part> and gives a <part>speech</part>: 'Lend me your bike, I'll bring it back by six.' No proof, no deposit. You hand it over anyway. That's <kanji>faith</kanji>.
信.on: At six on the dot he's back with your bike, limping: he banged his <sound>shin</sound> on the pedal.

刻.meaning: An <part>acrobat</part> tumbles across the room and, mid-flip, flicks a <part>dagger</part> at a block of wood. Scratch, scratch: each flip carves one more letter of her name. When she lands, it's there for good. She can <kanji>engrave</kanji> anything.
刻.on: A <sound>cock</sound>atoo lands on the block and pecks a curly tail onto the last letter.
刻.kun: Next she carves a <sound>key</sound> into the wood and sells it at the ba<sound>za</sound>ar.

走.meaning: Your feet kick up <part>soil</part> as you race down the track, one foot pushing off like a <part>skate</part> blade, long stride after long stride. Wind in your hair, heart pounding: you <kanji>run</kanji>.
走.on: Then you step on a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p and slide the rest of the way.
走.kun: You run past a <sound>hu</sound>t where a knight waves his <sound>shi</sound>eld and cheers you on.

起.meaning: A <part>runner</part> is fast asleep on the track when a <part>cobra</part> slithers over and hisses right in her ear. Her eyes snap open and she's off like a shot. Nothing will <kanji>rouse</kanji> you faster.
起.on: She had locked the cobra in a box, but it stole the <sound>key</sound>.
起.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she gasps as the cobra's tongue tickles her nose, and she leaps out of bed.

馬.meaning: A tall shape with a flowing mane gallops across a bed of <part>hot coals</part>, four hooves flicking up sparks. It snorts, it neighs, and it never once slows down. It's a brave <kanji>horse</kanji>.
馬.on: After its run, the coals are just right for a <sound>ba</sound>rbecue.
馬.kun: The horse slurps a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don and drinks tea from a giant <sound>mu</sound>g.

駅.meaning: Long ago a <part>horse</part> ran from town to town, and at every stop someone would <part>measure</part> out oats and water. Fresh horse in, tired horse out. Today the trains still stop at the same spot: the <kanji>station</kanji>.
駅.on: On the platform, a spiky <sound>ech</sound>idna waits for the next train.

返.meaning: You roll a ball up a <part>ramp</part>, but the ramp is <part>anti</part> everything: it shoves the ball straight back down to your feet. Up it goes again, and back it comes. Whatever you send, it will <kanji>return</kanji>.
返.on: A <sound>hen</sound> at the top kicks the ball back down with one claw.
返.kun: You give a <sound>ca</sound>rp back to the pond and an <sound>e</sound>gg back to the hen.

満.meaning: Rain falls in <part>water drops</part> on the pond until it rises over the <part>grass</part> at the edges, spilling out on <part>both</part> sides. Not one more drop will fit. The pond is <kanji>full</kanji>.
満.on: A thirsty <sound>mon</sound>key tries to drink it dry and gives up, its belly sloshing.
満.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands on tiptoe as the water fills up to its chin.

巾.meaning: A <part>pole</part> hangs down through a little <part>frame</part> on the bathroom wall, and something soft and fluffy drapes over it. Step out of the bath, reach over, rub your hair dry. It's a <kanji>towel</kanji>.
巾.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives into your bath and dries off on your towel.
巾.kun: You hang the towel over the kingfisher's cage under a big <sound>oa</sound>k tree: a cover.

席.meaning: In the corner of a <part>shed</part> there's an old crate with a <part>tray</part> on top and a folded <part>towel</part> for a cushion. Nobody else may sit there: it's Grandpa's, and he guards his <kanji>seat</kanji>.
席.on: He chalks a pie-chart <sound>sec</sound>tor on the floor around it, and nobody dares step inside.
席.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se, a knight with a <sound>shi</sound>eld and a <sound>ro</sound>dent squeeze onto the mat beside him: a straw mat.

座.meaning: Under a <part>shed</part> roof, two friends spread out a <part>picnic</part> on the ground and plop down knees up. No chairs needed, no table either. They <kanji>squat</kanji> by the sandwiches all afternoon.
座.on: They squat there like traders at a ba<sound>za</sound>ar, selling off spare sandwiches.
座.kun: They sit down to <sound>su</sound>shi, and a baby cries '<sound>Wa</sound>h!' until she gets some.

帰.meaning: After years at sea, a sailor walks in the door with a <part>dagger</part> on his belt. His mum doesn't hug him first: she grabs her <part>feather duster</part> and dusts him from hat to boots. Then the hug. What a <kanji>homecoming</kanji>.
帰.on: He has lost his front door <sound>key</sound>, so he knocks with the handle of his dagger.
帰.kun: Mum cooks him <sound>ca</sound>rp and a fried <sound>e</sound>gg, the dish he always loved as a boy.

市.meaning: A <part>lid</part> of cloth stretched on poles makes an awning, and a <part>towel</part> hangs below with prices pinned on it. Under it someone sells apples, someone sells socks, someone yells 'Two for one!'. Welcome to the <kanji>market</kanji>.
市.on: A knight haggles for a dented <sound>shi</sound>eld at half price.
市.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l sells fish at one stall, and a <sound>chee</sound>tah sells running shoes at the next.

姉.meaning: A <part>woman</part> marches you round the <part>market</part>, holding your hand tight and bossing you: 'Don't touch! Stay close!' She was born three years before you and never lets you forget it. She's your <kanji>elder sister</kanji>.
姉.on: She even bosses the knight at the stall: 'Polish that <sound>shi</sound>eld!'
姉.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, stop!' she yells, and catches you in a butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t before you can run off.

婦.meaning: On a packed train, a <part>woman</part> in white gloves pulls a <part>feather duster</part> from her handbag, dusts her seat before she sits, then dusts the seat beside her for a tired stranger. Not a crumb, not a rude word, a smile for everyone. A true <kanji>lady</kanji>.
婦.on: She even dusts the rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton a backpacker has wedged into the luggage rack.
婦.kun: Her stop is a wedding: she gets off with a <sound>yo</sound>gurt cake and a long <sound>me</sound>nu for the bride.

布.meaning: With one <part>slash</part> of her scissors and <part>one</part> straight cut, a tailor trims a <part>towel</part>-sized piece from a roll. Smooth, cool and a little crinkly, it isn't cotton at all. It's fine <kanji>linen</kanji>.
布.on: She sews the linen into a crisp cover for a <sound>fu</sound>ton.
布.kun: She keeps the cloth in a reading <sound>noo</sound>k, and when the cat climbs on it she shouts '<sound>No</sound>!'

役.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> runs the <part>chairlift</part> on the mountain: she checks every bar, waves every skier on, and brushes the snow off every seat. Rain or shine, she never leaves her post. It's her <kanji>duty</kanji>.
役.on: Her other job is watering a spiky <sound>yuc</sound>ca at the top of the lift.

示.meaning: A tour guide climbs onto a crate made of <part>two</part> planks and holds up a <part>little</part> sign on a stick. 'Look over there!' she points. 'And there! And there!' Her whole job is to <kanji>show</kanji> you things.
示.on: She drives the group around in a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p, pointing out of the window.
示.kun: In the castle she points to a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld, then to a <sound>me</sound>dal in a glass case.

禁.meaning: Deep in a <part>grove</part> stands an old stone <part>altar</part>, and a sign nailed to a tree says KEEP OUT. No picnics, no climbing, no touching. Anyone who steps closer breaks the <kanji>prohibition</kanji>.
禁.on: Only a <sound>kin</sound>gfisher ignores the sign and perches right on the altar.

衣.meaning: A <part>lid</part> on top like a collar, and below it the cloth swings open and flares out at the hem. Hang it on a hook, slip your arms in, tie the belt. It's a <kanji>garment</kanji>.
衣.on: As you put it on, an <sound>ee</sound>l wriggles out of the sleeve.
衣.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala sews a robe for a <sound>ro</sound>dent out of an old <sound>mo</sound>ccasin.

表.meaning: A tailor stitches <part>two</part> stripes and a <part>pole</part> of buttons onto the outside of a <part>garment</part>. The rough seams stay hidden inside, and only the neat side faces the world. That's its <kanji>surface</kanji>.
表.on: A dancer in one tall <sound>hee</sound>l spins a <sound>yo</sound>-yo across the shiny surface.
表.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' you spot a muddy <sound>mo</sound>ccasin print on the outside of your <sound>te</sound>nt.

変.meaning: A <part>jellyfish</part> wobbles up the beach and sits down in a <part>folding chair</part>, puts on sunglasses and orders a lemonade. The other sunbathers stare. You don't see that every day. Very <kanji>unusual</kanji>.
変.on: Then a <sound>hen</sound> sits down in the next chair and orders the same.
変.kun: Next day the jellyfish has changed into a <sound>ca</sound>rp, still in the same chair.

危.meaning: An <part>unlucky</part> man stands at the edge of a cliff throwing a <part>boomerang</part>. It swings wide, turns, and comes whistling straight back at his head. He ducks, wobbles, nearly falls. This hobby is <kanji>dangerous</kanji>.
危.on: As he ducks, his car <sound>key</sound> slips out of his pocket and over the edge.
危.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' he shouts, as a runaway <sound>bu</sound>lldozer rolls toward the cliff edge too.

公.meaning: <part>Eight</part> strangers stand elbow to <part>elbow</part> around a park fountain that belongs to nobody and everybody. Anyone can sit on its benches, drink from it or splash in it. It's <kanji>public</kanji>.
公.on: All eight line up for an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne from the van by the gate.
公.kun: Under a big <sound>oa</sound>k, a park stall sells balls of <sound>ya</sound>rn and squirts of <sound>ke</sound>tchup to anyone at all.

青.meaning: A <part>TV antenna</part> on a rooftop points up at the <part>moon</part>, but the night is so clear that the sky never goes black. It stays a deep, glowing <kanji>blue</kanji> all the way to dawn.
青.on: Even the steel <sound>sa</sound>fe in the attic has been painted blue to match.
青.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>… <sound>oh</sound>!' you sigh, then gasp, at how blue the sky is.

晴.meaning: A grumpy man stomps through town under a huge umbrella, moaning about the rain. A kid tugs his sleeve and points: the <part>sun</part> is out, people are in shorts, the sky is <part>blue</part> from edge to edge. He peeks out and blinks. It decided to <kanji>clear up</kanji> an hour ago.
晴.on: Red-faced, he folds the umbrella and locks it away in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe.
晴.kun: He hides in a beach <sound>hu</sound>t, the only one in town still dripping wet.

広.meaning: You stick out an <part>elbow</part> in your old <part>shed</part> and hit nothing. Stretch both arms: still nothing. The walls seem miles away, and there's room for a tractor. This shed is <kanji>wide</kanji>.
広.on: There's room to park an ice cream van inside and sell a <sound>co</sound>ne to everyone.
広.kun: In high <sound>hee</sound>ls, a <sound>ro</sound>dent tap-dances from one far wall to the other.
